Tuberculosis.overview: Tuberculosis (TB) is an infectious disease caused by bacteria. It most commonly affects the lungs but can also affect other parts of the body. TB is preventable and curable with appropriate medical care.
general_guidance: Seek medical evaluation if you have a persistent cough, fever or unexplained weight loss.
A healthcare professional may recommend appropriate tests to determine whether TB is present.
If diagnosed, follow the treatment plan prescribed by your healthcare professional.
Do not stop prescribed TB treatment without medical advice.
Cover your mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing, and maintain good ventilation.

Allergic sinusitis.overview: The dataset uses the label Allergic sinusitis. Allergy-related nasal symptoms are commonly described as allergic rhinitis, which occurs when the nose reacts to allergens such as pollen, dust mites or mould.
general_guidance: Try to identify and avoid triggers that cause your symptoms.
Keep indoor spaces clean and well ventilated.
A pharmacist or healthcare professional can advise on suitable symptom relief.
Seek medical advice if symptoms worsen or affect your daily activities.
urgent_warning_signs: Sudden swelling of the lips, tongue or throat
Difficulty swallowing or feeling that the throat is closing

Acute rhinosinusitis.overview: Acute rhinosinusitis involves inflammation and swelling of the lining of the nose and sinuses. It commonly occurs after a cold or flu and is often caused by an infection.
common_symptoms: Pain or tenderness around the cheeks, eyes or forehead
general_guidance: Get adequate rest and drink enough fluids.
Avoid smoking and exposure to irritants.
Saline nasal rinses may help relieve nasal congestion.
Consult a healthcare professional if symptoms persist, recur or worsen.
urgent_warning_signs: Severe symptoms in someone with a weakened immune system

Influenza.overview: Influenza, commonly called flu, is a contagious respiratory illness caused by influenza viruses. Symptoms often begin suddenly and can range from mild to severe.
general_guidance: Get adequate rest and drink enough fluids.
Stay home and limit close contact with others while unwell.
Maintain hand hygiene and improve indoor ventilation.
Contact a healthcare professional if symptoms are severe or you are at increased risk of complications.
urgent_warning_signs: Difficulty breathing or shortness of breath
Persistent chest or abdominal pain or pressure
Fever or cough that improves but then returns or worsens
Influenza.source_name: CDC - Signs and Symptoms of Flu

Pneumonia.overview: Pneumonia is an acute respiratory infection that can be caused by viruses or bacteria. It affects the lungs and can cause difficulty breathing. Severity varies from mild to life-threatening.
general_guidance: Seek medical evaluation if pneumonia is suspected.
Follow the treatment plan prescribed by a qualified healthcare professional.
Get adequate rest and maintain hydration.
Maintain hand hygiene and discuss appropriate vaccinations with a healthcare professional.

URTI.overview: An upper respiratory tract infection affects parts of the respiratory system such as the nose, sinuses and throat. Many respiratory infections improve over time, although some require medical assessment.
general_guidance: Get adequate rest and drink enough water.
Maintain hand hygiene and cover your mouth when coughing or sneezing.
Avoid close contact with others while unwell.
Consult a healthcare professional if symptoms persist, worsen or cause concern.
urgent_warning_signs: Symptoms that improve and then become significantly worse

Bronchitis.overview: Bronchitis is inflammation of the airways in the lungs. Acute bronchitis is commonly caused by a viral infection and usually improves on its own.
common_symptoms: Persistent cough, with or without mucus
general_guidance: Get adequate rest and drink plenty of fluids.
Avoid smoking and exposure to smoke.
A healthcare professional can assess symptoms and recommend appropriate care.
Antibiotics do not usually help when bronchitis is caused by a virus.
Seek medical advice if the cough lasts more than three weeks or symptoms worsen.
urgent_warning_signs: Blue or grey lips or skin

Viral pharyngitis.overview: Viral pharyngitis is inflammation of the throat caused by a viral infection. It commonly occurs with cold or flu-like illnesses. Most viral sore throats improve within about one week.
general_guidance: Drink adequate fluids.
Get sufficient rest.
Avoid smoking and exposure to throat irritants.
A healthcare professional can assess persistent or worsening symptoms.
Antibiotics do not treat viral infections.
urgent_warning_signs: Inability to swallow fluids or saliva
Viral pharyngitis.source_name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

Acute otitis media.overview: Acute otitis media is a sudden infection or inflammation of the middle ear. It is particularly common in children and can occur after a cold or other respiratory infection.
common_symptoms: Feeling of pressure or fullness in the ear
Fluid or discharge from the ear
Irritability or disturbed sleep in children
general_guidance: Seek medical advice if ear pain persists or symptoms worsen.
A healthcare professional can examine the ear and determine appropriate care.
Many uncomplicated ear infections improve without antibiotics.
Do not insert cotton buds or other objects into the ear.
Follow a healthcare professional's advice about suitable pain relief.
urgent_warning_signs: Swelling around or behind the ear
Fluid or pus coming from the ear
Very high fever or feeling seriously unwell

Chronic rhinosinusitis.overview: Chronic rhinosinusitis is long-lasting inflammation of the lining of the nose and sinuses. It can cause persistent nasal blockage and facial discomfort, with symptoms lasting for several months.
common_symptoms: Mucus dripping down the back of the throat
general_guidance: Consult a healthcare professional if symptoms persist for several months.
A healthcare professional may recommend saline nasal rinses or other suitable treatment.
Avoid known triggers such as smoke and other nasal irritants.
Follow the treatment plan recommended by your healthcare professional.
An ENT specialist may be needed for persistent or recurrent symptoms.
urgent_warning_signs: Swelling or redness around the eyes
Confusion or other significant neurological symptoms

Bronchiolitis.overview: Bronchiolitis is a common viral chest infection affecting the small airways in the lungs. It mainly affects babies and children under two years of age and can sometimes become serious.
general_guidance: Monitor the child's breathing and feeding.
Offer appropriate fluids or smaller, more frequent feeds.
Keep the child away from cigarette smoke.
Seek medical advice if feeding decreases or symptoms worsen.
Follow a healthcare professional's advice, especially for young babies.
urgent_warning_signs: Blue or grey lips, tongue or skin

Spontaneous pneumothorax.overview: A spontaneous pneumothorax occurs when air leaks into the space between the lung and chest wall, causing part or all of the lung to collapse. It can happen without an obvious injury and requires prompt medical assessment.
common_symptoms: Sudden sharp chest pain, usually on one side
Chest pain that worsens during deep breathing
general_guidance: Seek immediate medical assessment if you experience sudden chest pain or breathlessness.
A healthcare professional may recommend a chest X-ray or other imaging.
Treatment depends on the size of the pneumothorax and the person's symptoms.
Some cases require hospital observation, while others need removal of trapped air.
Avoid smoking and follow medical advice about physical activity, flying and diving.
urgent_warning_signs: Blue or grey lips or skin

Cluster headache.overview: Cluster headache is a type of headache that causes repeated attacks of severe pain, usually around one eye or one side of the head. Attacks may occur several times a day during periods lasting weeks or months.
common_symptoms: Severe sharp or burning pain around one eye
Pain on one side of the head
Blocked or runny nose on the affected side
Swelling or drooping of the eyelid
general_guidance: Consult a healthcare professional if you experience repeated severe headaches.
Keep a headache diary to record the timing, duration and possible triggers.
Avoid identified triggers where possible.
A healthcare professional may recommend specialist treatment to manage or prevent attacks.
Do not assume a new or unusually severe headache is a cluster headache without medical assessment.
urgent_warning_signs: New drooping eyelid or unequal pupil size

Boerhaave.overview: Boerhaave syndrome is a rare but serious condition involving a full-thickness tear in the oesophagus (food pipe). It often occurs after forceful vomiting or retching. It is a medical emergency because contents can leak into the chest and cause severe infection.
common_symptoms: Pain in the neck or back
Vomiting or a history of forceful retching
general_guidance: Suspected Boerhaave syndrome requires immediate emergency medical assessment.
Do not wait for symptoms to improve on their own.
Emergency hospital assessment and imaging may be required.
Treatment may involve specialist procedures or surgery.
Follow the emergency medical team's instructions.
urgent_warning_signs: Severe chest pain after forceful vomiting
Fainting, confusion or signs of shock

Spontaneous rib fracture.overview: A spontaneous rib fracture is a break in a rib that can occur without a major injury. It may sometimes result from repeated severe coughing or weakened bones, such as in people with osteoporosis. Medical assessment is important to check for associated injuries and underlying causes.
common_symptoms: Pain in the rib or chest area
Pain that worsens during deep breathing
Discomfort when pressing the affected area
general_guidance: Seek medical assessment for unexplained rib pain or suspected fracture.
A healthcare professional may recommend imaging to assess the injury.
Follow professional advice about pain management and activity.
Avoid activities that worsen the pain while recovering.
A healthcare professional may assess bone health or other underlying causes.
urgent_warning_signs: Chest pressure or pain spreading to the arm, jaw or back

GERD.overview: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) occurs when stomach contents repeatedly flow back into the oesophagus (food pipe). This can cause irritation and discomfort, particularly after meals or when lying down.
common_symptoms: Heartburn or burning sensation in the chest
Acid or sour taste in the mouth
general_guidance: Consider eating smaller meals and avoiding meals close to bedtime.
Notice whether particular foods or drinks trigger symptoms.
Avoid lying down immediately after eating.
Seek medical advice if symptoms occur frequently or persist.
A healthcare professional can recommend appropriate treatment if needed.
urgent_warning_signs: Chest pain with breathlessness or sweating

HIV (initial infection).overview: HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) attacks the immune system. During the initial stage, some people develop flu-like symptoms, while others may have no noticeable symptoms. Symptoms alone cannot confirm HIV infection; testing is necessary.
general_guidance: If you think you may have been exposed to HIV, seek medical advice and testing promptly.
If a possible exposure occurred within the last 72 hours, seek urgent medical care to discuss post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP).
A healthcare professional can recommend the appropriate HIV test.
An early negative test may need to be repeated after the test-specific window period.
If HIV is confirmed, effective treatment is available and should be started under medical supervision.
Avoid sharing needles or other injection equipment.

Anemia.overview: Anemia is a condition in which the blood has a lower-than-normal haemoglobin level or an insufficient number of healthy red blood cells. This can reduce the amount of oxygen carried to body tissues. It may have several causes, including nutritional deficiencies, blood loss and underlying illnesses.
general_guidance: Consult a healthcare professional to identify the underlying cause.
A blood test, such as a complete blood count, may be recommended.
Treatment depends on the type and cause of anemia.
Maintain a balanced diet containing appropriate sources of iron, vitamin B12 and folate.
Do not start iron supplements without appropriate medical advice.

Inguinal hernia.overview: An inguinal hernia occurs when tissue, often part of the intestine, pushes through a weak area in the lower abdominal wall near the groin. It may cause a visible or noticeable bulge that can become more prominent when coughing, bending or lifting.
common_symptoms: A bulge in the groin area
Discomfort or pain in the groin
A dragging or heavy sensation in the groin
Pain that increases when coughing or lifting
A bulge that becomes more noticeable when standing
general_guidance: Consult a healthcare professional if you notice a groin lump or persistent groin discomfort.
A physical examination is commonly used to assess a suspected hernia.
Treatment depends on the size of the hernia, symptoms and overall health.
Avoid activities that cause significant pain until you receive medical advice.
A healthcare professional can discuss whether monitoring or surgery is appropriate.
urgent_warning_signs: Sudden severe pain in the groin
A painful lump that becomes firm or cannot be pushed back
Redness or darkening of the skin over the lump
Abdominal swelling or inability to pass stool or gas

Myasthenia gravis.overview: Myasthenia gravis is a long-term autoimmune condition that affects communication between nerves and muscles. It causes muscle weakness that often becomes worse with activity and improves after rest. It commonly affects the eyes, face, throat and limbs.
common_symptoms: Drooping of one or both eyelids
Weakness in the arms or legs
Muscle weakness that worsens with activity
general_guidance: Seek assessment from a healthcare professional if you experience unexplained or fluctuating muscle weakness.
A neurologist may recommend tests to evaluate nerve and muscle function.
Treatment is available to help manage symptoms.
Follow the treatment plan prescribed by your healthcare professional.
Discuss infections, new medicines and worsening weakness with your healthcare team.

Whooping cough.overview: Whooping cough, also called pertussis, is a contagious respiratory infection caused by the bacterium Bordetella pertussis. It often begins with cold-like symptoms and can develop into severe coughing fits. It can be particularly dangerous for babies and young children.
common_symptoms: A high-pitched whooping sound while breathing in
general_guidance: Seek medical advice if you or your child develop persistent or severe coughing fits.
Early medical assessment is important, especially for babies and pregnant people.
A healthcare professional may recommend testing and appropriate treatment.
Follow prescribed treatment and advice about preventing the spread of infection.
Keep away from vulnerable people until a healthcare professional advises that it is safe.
Vaccination helps protect against whooping cough.
urgent_warning_signs: Pauses in breathing, especially in babies
Blue or grey lips or skin
Whooping cough.source_name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

Anaphylaxis.overview: Anaphylaxis is a severe, rapidly developing allergic reaction that can be life-threatening. It may occur after exposure to certain foods, medicines or insect stings. It can affect breathing, circulation and multiple body systems.
common_symptoms: Sudden swelling of the lips, tongue or throat
Tightness in the throat or difficulty swallowing
Raised, itchy skin rash or hives
general_guidance: Suspected anaphylaxis is a medical emergency. Do not wait for symptoms to improve.
Use a prescribed adrenaline auto-injector immediately if available, following its instructions.
Call emergency services immediately. In India, call 112.
Follow the emergency operator's instructions while waiting for help.
Even if symptoms improve after adrenaline, emergency hospital assessment is still necessary.
urgent_warning_signs: Sudden swelling of the mouth, tongue or throat
Throat tightness or inability to swallow
Blue, grey or unusually pale lips or skin
Sudden confusion, collapse or loss of consciousness

Epiglottitis.overview: Epiglottitis is inflammation and swelling of the epiglottis, the flap of tissue that helps prevent food and liquid from entering the windpipe. Severe swelling can obstruct the airway, making this a medical emergency.
general_guidance: Suspected epiglottitis requires immediate emergency medical attention.
Call emergency services immediately. In India, call 112.
Keep the person calm and in a comfortable upright position.
Do not try to examine the throat or force anything into the mouth.
Do not attempt to manage suspected epiglottitis with home remedies.
Hospital treatment and airway monitoring may be necessary.
urgent_warning_signs: Drooling or inability to swallow saliva
Blue or grey lips or skin

Guillain-Barré syndrome.overview: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) is a rare neurological condition in which the immune system attacks the peripheral nerves. It can cause tingling, numbness and progressive muscle weakness, sometimes affecting the muscles responsible for breathing and swallowing.
common_symptoms: Tingling or pins and needles in the feet and hands
Muscle weakness beginning in the legs
Weakness that spreads to the arms or upper body
Nerve pain in the legs or back
general_guidance: Seek urgent medical assessment if Guillain-Barré syndrome is suspected.
People with suspected GBS generally require hospital assessment and close monitoring.
Healthcare professionals may monitor breathing, heart rate and blood pressure.
Treatment may include intravenous immunoglobulin or plasma exchange.
Follow specialist medical advice and rehabilitation recommendations.
urgent_warning_signs: Inability to walk or move normally

Acute laryngitis.overview: Acute laryngitis is short-term inflammation of the voice box (larynx), causing irritation or swelling of the vocal cords. It commonly occurs with viral infections such as colds and usually improves within one to two weeks.
general_guidance: Rest your voice and avoid unnecessary talking.
Drink plenty of fluids.
Avoid shouting, whispering and smoking because they can strain or irritate the voice.
Avoid smoky and dusty environments.
Seek medical advice if symptoms do not improve after two weeks or repeatedly return.
A healthcare professional can assess persistent voice changes.

Croup.overview: Croup is a respiratory condition that mainly affects babies and young children. It causes swelling around the voice box and windpipe, leading to a characteristic barking cough and sometimes noisy breathing. It is often associated with a viral infection.
common_symptoms: High-pitched or rasping sound while breathing in
Symptoms that may become worse at night
general_guidance: Seek medical advice if you think a child may have croup.
Keep the child calm because distress and crying can worsen breathing symptoms.
Keep the child comfortably upright.
Offer appropriate fluids.
Monitor breathing and general condition, including during the night.
Do not use steam inhalation as a treatment.
Follow a healthcare professional's advice about treatment.
urgent_warning_signs: Chest or abdomen pulling inward during breathing
Blue, grey or unusually pale lips or skin
Severe restlessness accompanied by breathing difficulty

PSVT.overview: PSVT is a type of abnormal heart rhythm in which the heart suddenly starts beating much faster than normal. Episodes may begin and end abruptly and can last from a few minutes to several hours.
general_guidance: Seek medical assessment if you experience repeated episodes of a suddenly rapid heartbeat.
An electrocardiogram (ECG) may be needed to identify the heart rhythm.
A healthcare professional can advise whether monitoring, medication or other treatment is appropriate.
Reduce possible triggers such as excessive caffeine if they appear to affect your symptoms.
Follow any heart-rhythm management plan provided by your healthcare professional.
urgent_warning_signs: Rapid heartbeat accompanied by chest pain
Fainting or feeling close to fainting
An episode that lasts longer than usual and causes significant symptoms

Atrial fibrillation.overview: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a heart rhythm condition in which the heartbeat becomes irregular and often faster than normal. It can increase the risk of blood clots and stroke, so proper medical assessment and management are important.
general_guidance: Seek medical assessment if you notice a persistent or recurring irregular heartbeat.
An ECG is commonly used to confirm an abnormal heart rhythm.
A healthcare professional may assess your risk of stroke and discuss suitable treatment.
Treatment may include medicines to control heart rate or rhythm and reduce blood clot risk.
Take prescribed medicines as directed and attend recommended follow-up appointments.
urgent_warning_signs: Sudden weakness or numbness on one side of the body
Sudden difficulty speaking or understanding speech
Sudden loss or blurring of vision

Bronchiectasis.overview: Bronchiectasis is a long-term lung condition in which the airways become abnormally widened and damaged. This can cause mucus to build up, increasing the risk of repeated chest infections. Treatment can help manage symptoms and reduce complications.
general_guidance: Consult a healthcare professional if you have a persistent cough or repeated chest infections.
A healthcare professional may recommend sputum testing, lung function tests or chest imaging.
A respiratory physiotherapist may teach techniques to help clear mucus from the lungs.
Follow the treatment plan prescribed for any chest infection.
Avoid smoking and follow recommended vaccination advice.
Attend regular medical reviews to monitor the condition.
urgent_warning_signs: Coughing up more than small streaks of blood
Chest pain with fever or worsening infection symptoms
Blue or grey lips or skin

Chagas.overview: Chagas disease, also known as American trypanosomiasis, is an infection caused by the parasite Trypanosoma cruzi. It is mainly transmitted by infected triatomine insects, but can also spread through contaminated food or drink, blood transfusions, organ transplantation and from mother to baby. Many people have mild or no symptoms initially.
common_symptoms: Swelling around the site of infection
Swelling of one eyelid in some cases
general_guidance: Seek medical assessment if you may have been exposed to Chagas disease.
Tell your healthcare professional about relevant travel, residence or exposure history.
Blood tests may be recommended to check for infection.
Antiparasitic treatment is available and is generally most effective when started early.
People with confirmed infection may need follow-up to assess heart or digestive complications.
Follow specialist medical advice and prescribed treatment.

Scombroid food poisoning.overview: Scombroid poisoning is a type of food poisoning caused by eating fish that contains high levels of histamine due to improper storage or refrigeration. Symptoms often begin within minutes to an hour after eating contaminated fish and can resemble an allergic reaction.
common_symptoms: Flushing of the face or upper body
general_guidance: Seek medical advice if symptoms develop after eating fish.
Tell the healthcare professional what fish was eaten and when symptoms started.
A healthcare professional may recommend antihistamine treatment.
Do not eat more of the suspected contaminated fish.
Other people who ate the same fish may also need medical assessment.
Prevent scombroid poisoning by ensuring fish is stored and refrigerated properly.
urgent_warning_signs: Swelling of the tongue or throat
Signs of low blood pressure or collapse
Scombroid food poisoning.source_name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

Myocarditis.overview: Myocarditis is inflammation of the heart muscle (myocardium). It can affect the heart's ability to pump blood and may occur after an infection or due to other causes. Severity ranges from mild to serious.
general_guidance: Seek prompt medical assessment if myocarditis is suspected.
A healthcare professional may recommend an ECG, blood tests, echocardiogram or cardiac MRI.
Treatment depends on the cause and severity of the condition.
Follow medical advice about physical activity and exercise; strenuous exercise may need to be avoided during active inflammation.
Attend recommended follow-up appointments to monitor heart function.
urgent_warning_signs: Rapid or irregular heartbeat accompanied by dizziness

Larygospasm.overview: Laryngospasm is a sudden involuntary tightening or closure of the vocal cords. This can temporarily restrict airflow and make it difficult to breathe or speak. Possible triggers include acid reflux, airway irritation and certain medical procedures.
general_guidance: Seek medical assessment for repeated or unexplained episodes.
A healthcare professional may assess possible triggers such as acid reflux or airway conditions.
An ENT specialist may examine the vocal cords when necessary.
Follow professional advice about managing any underlying condition.
Do not assume that every episode of breathing difficulty is laryngospasm.
urgent_warning_signs: Inability to speak because of breathing difficulty
Blue or grey lips or skin

Acute dystonic reactions.overview: Acute dystonic reactions are sudden, involuntary muscle contractions that can cause abnormal movements or sustained postures. They are commonly associated with certain medicines, including some antipsychotic and anti-nausea medicines, particularly after starting treatment or increasing a dose.
common_symptoms: Unusual twisting or turning of the head
Jaw tightness or difficulty opening the mouth
Muscle spasms in the arms or legs
general_guidance: Seek prompt medical assessment if sudden involuntary muscle contractions develop.
Tell the healthcare professional about all recently started medicines and dose changes.
Do not take additional doses of a suspected triggering medicine until you have received medical advice.
A healthcare professional can assess the reaction and decide on appropriate treatment.
Record the suspected medicine reaction and discuss it with your prescribing healthcare professional.

Localized edema.overview: Localized edema refers to swelling caused by excess fluid collecting in a particular part of the body. It can affect areas such as the feet, ankles, legs, hands or face. Possible causes include injury, infection, inflammation, blood clots and problems affecting circulation.
common_symptoms: Swelling in a specific body area
Reduced movement in the affected area
A temporary indentation after pressing the swollen area
Redness or warmth in some cases
general_guidance: Seek medical assessment if swelling is unexplained, persistent or worsening.
The appropriate treatment depends on the underlying cause.
Avoid remaining seated or standing in the same position for prolonged periods.
Gentle movement or elevating the affected limb may help some types of swelling, when appropriate.
Do not assume unexplained swelling is harmless, particularly if it affects only one limb.
urgent_warning_signs: Swelling accompanied by severe pain, redness or warmth
Swelling in one leg accompanied by breathlessness
Swelling of the face, lips or tongue with breathing difficulty

SLE.overview: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a long-term autoimmune condition in which the immune system mistakenly attacks healthy tissues. It can affect several parts of the body, including the joints, skin, kidneys, heart and lungs. Symptoms can vary and often occur in flare-ups.
common_symptoms: Skin rashes, sometimes across the cheeks and nose
general_guidance: Consult a healthcare professional if you experience persistent joint pain, unexplained rashes or recurring fatigue.
Diagnosis may involve medical history, physical examination, blood tests and urine tests.
Treatment depends on the organs affected and the severity of the condition.
Protect your skin from excessive sunlight if you experience photosensitivity.
Follow your prescribed treatment and attend regular medical reviews.
Do not stop prescribed medication without medical advice.
urgent_warning_signs: Chest pain or severe difficulty breathing
Severe headache with confusion or neurological changes
Sudden weakness or loss of movement

Unstable angina.overview: Unstable angina is a serious heart condition in which the heart muscle does not receive enough blood and oxygen. Chest discomfort may occur unexpectedly, at rest, or become more frequent, severe or prolonged. It is an acute coronary syndrome and requires emergency medical assessment.
common_symptoms: Pain that lasts longer than usual
Pain that becomes more frequent or severe
Pain spreading to the arms, shoulders, neck, jaw or back
general_guidance: Suspected unstable angina requires immediate emergency medical assessment.
Call emergency services. In India, call 112.
Stop physical activity and rest while waiting for emergency help.
Do not drive yourself to the hospital.
Hospital assessment may include an ECG and blood tests to check for a heart attack.
Follow the treatment and monitoring plan provided by the cardiac care team.
urgent_warning_signs: Chest pressure that does not settle
Pain spreading to the arm, jaw, neck or back
Chest pain accompanied by sweating or nausea

Stable angina.overview: Stable angina is chest discomfort caused by reduced blood flow to the heart muscle. It commonly follows a predictable pattern and may occur during physical activity, emotional stress or exposure to cold. It often improves with rest or prescribed angina medication.
common_symptoms: Pain spreading to the arms, shoulders, neck or jaw
general_guidance: Arrange medical assessment if you experience recurring chest discomfort.
A healthcare professional may recommend an ECG and other heart investigations.
Follow your prescribed angina action plan and use prescribed medication as directed.
Stop the activity that triggers symptoms and rest.
Discuss suitable exercise, diet and lifestyle changes with your healthcare professional.
Seek emergency care if chest pain becomes new, more severe, prolonged or occurs at rest.
urgent_warning_signs: Chest pain that is new or more severe than usual
Chest discomfort that does not improve with rest or prescribed medication
Pain spreading to the arm, jaw, neck or back
Chest pain accompanied by sweating, nausea or severe breathlessness
Stable angina.source_name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI)

Ebola.overview: Ebola disease is a rare but severe infectious illness caused by viruses belonging to the orthoebolavirus group. It can spread through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of an infected person who is showing symptoms, or contaminated materials. Symptoms usually begin between 2 and 21 days after exposure. Early symptoms can resemble other common infections, so exposure history and laboratory testing are important.
general_guidance: If you have compatible symptoms after possible exposure to Ebola, contact public health or medical authorities immediately.
Tell healthcare professionals about relevant travel, contact and exposure history.
Avoid direct contact with other people's blood or body fluids.
Do not visit healthcare facilities without first informing them of suspected exposure, so appropriate infection-control arrangements can be made.
Laboratory testing is necessary to confirm Ebola disease.
Early supportive medical care is important.
urgent_warning_signs: Fever following possible exposure to Ebola
Severe or persistent vomiting or diarrhea

Acute pulmonary edema.overview: Acute pulmonary edema is a sudden buildup of fluid in the lungs that interferes with normal breathing and oxygen exchange. It is often associated with heart problems, including acute heart failure, and requires immediate hospital assessment.
common_symptoms: Cough with frothy or pink-tinged sputum
A feeling of suffocation or drowning
general_guidance: Suspected acute pulmonary edema is a medical emergency.
Call emergency services immediately. In India, call 112.
Do not attempt to manage sudden severe breathing difficulty at home.
Keep the person as comfortable as possible while waiting for emergency assistance.
Hospital treatment may include oxygen or breathing support and treatment of the underlying cause.
Follow the medical team's instructions and monitoring plan.
urgent_warning_signs: Blue or grey lips or skin

Pulmonary embolism.overview: A pulmonary embolism occurs when a blood clot blocks a blood vessel in the lungs. The clot often travels from a deep vein in the leg or, less commonly, another part of the body. It can be life-threatening and requires urgent medical treatment.
common_symptoms: Chest pain that may worsen when breathing in
Pain or swelling in one leg
general_guidance: Suspected pulmonary embolism requires urgent hospital assessment.
Call emergency services immediately if sudden breathlessness or chest pain occurs. In India, call 112.
Do not drive yourself to the hospital.
A healthcare professional may recommend blood tests and imaging to investigate a possible clot.
Treatment commonly involves anticoagulant medicines prescribed by a healthcare professional.
Take prescribed medicines exactly as directed and attend follow-up appointments.
urgent_warning_signs: Chest pain or upper back pain
Sudden breathlessness with one-sided leg swelling

Panic attack.overview: A panic attack is a sudden episode of intense fear or discomfort accompanied by physical and emotional symptoms. It can occur unexpectedly or in response to a stressful situation. Similar symptoms can also occur in medical conditions, so a first or unusual episode should not automatically be assumed to be a panic attack.
common_symptoms: Shortness of breath or rapid breathing
Fear of losing control or dying
general_guidance: Try to remain in a safe and comfortable place.
Breathe slowly and gently if you are able to do so.
Remind yourself that the intense feeling may pass.
Speak with a healthcare professional if panic attacks recur or affect daily activities.
Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) is one treatment option for panic disorder.
A healthcare professional should assess new or unexplained physical symptoms before attributing them to anxiety.
urgent_warning_signs: New, severe or persistent chest pain
Symptoms that are significantly different from previous episodes
Thoughts of self-harm or immediate risk of harm

Bronchospasm / acute asthma exacerbation.overview: Bronchospasm occurs when the muscles surrounding the airways tighten, narrowing the passages through which air moves. During an asthma exacerbation, airway inflammation and narrowing can make breathing difficult. An asthma attack can range from mild to life-threatening.
common_symptoms: Symptoms that worsen at night or early in the morning
general_guidance: Follow the personal asthma action plan provided by a healthcare professional.
Use prescribed reliever medication according to the action plan.
Sit upright and try to remain calm during breathing difficulty.
Avoid known triggers when possible, such as smoke, dust or other identified irritants.
Arrange medical review if symptoms are worsening or prescribed medication is needed more frequently.
Seek emergency assistance if symptoms are severe or do not improve according to the action plan.
urgent_warning_signs: Unable to speak in complete sentences because of breathlessness
Reliever medication not providing the expected improvement
Blue or grey lips or skin

Acute COPD exacerbation / infection.overview: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a group of lung conditions that cause persistent breathing difficulties. An exacerbation, or flare-up, is a sudden worsening of usual symptoms. Respiratory infections can trigger flare-ups, although other factors may also contribute.
common_symptoms: Change in phlegm colour or thickness
Fever or symptoms of a respiratory infection
general_guidance: Contact a healthcare professional when symptoms suddenly worsen.
Follow the COPD action plan provided by your healthcare team.
Use prescribed inhalers and other medicines only as directed.
Avoid cigarette smoke and other respiratory irritants.
Seek medical assessment if you notice increased breathlessness or changes in mucus.
Severe flare-ups may require urgent hospital treatment.
urgent_warning_signs: Difficulty speaking because of breathing problems
Blue or grey lips or skin

Pulmonary neoplasm.overview: A pulmonary neoplasm is an abnormal growth or tumour in the lung. It may be benign or malignant. Lung cancer is a malignant pulmonary neoplasm. Symptoms vary depending on the type, location and stage of the growth, and some people may have no symptoms in the early stages.
common_symptoms: Persistent cough that does not improve
general_guidance: Arrange medical assessment for a persistent cough, unexplained weight loss or other concerning symptoms.
A healthcare professional may recommend chest imaging and further investigations.
A suspected lung tumour requires appropriate specialist assessment.
Avoid tobacco smoke and seek support to stop smoking if needed.
Follow the investigation and treatment plan recommended by the healthcare team.
Symptoms alone cannot establish whether a lung growth is benign or malignant.
urgent_warning_signs: Significant or repeated coughing up of blood

Possible NSTEMI / STEMI.overview: NSTEMI and STEMI are types of heart attack, also called myocardial infarction. They occur when blood flow to part of the heart muscle is significantly reduced or blocked. STEMI is generally associated with a complete blockage of a coronary artery, while NSTEMI involves a different pattern of reduced blood flow. Both require immediate emergency medical assessment.
common_symptoms: Pain spreading to one or both arms
Pain in the jaw, neck, back or upper abdomen
general_guidance: Suspected heart attack is a medical emergency. Call emergency services immediately. In India, call 112.
Do not wait for symptoms to disappear or attempt to diagnose the type of heart attack at home.
Stop physical activity and follow instructions from emergency medical personnel.
Do not drive yourself to the hospital.
Hospital evaluation may include an ECG, blood tests such as troponin, and imaging or other investigations.
Treatment must be determined by the emergency and cardiac care team.
urgent_warning_signs: Chest pressure, squeezing or pain lasting more than a few minutes or returning repeatedly
Chest discomfort spreading to the arms, jaw, neck or back
Nausea or vomiting accompanied by chest discomfort

Sarcoidosis.overview: Sarcoidosis is an inflammatory condition in which small clusters of immune cells, called granulomas, develop in different organs. It most commonly affects the lungs and lymph nodes, but can also affect the skin, eyes, heart and other organs. Symptoms vary depending on the organs involved.
common_symptoms: Redness or pain in the eyes
general_guidance: Consult a healthcare professional for persistent respiratory symptoms, unexplained fatigue or unusual skin changes.
Diagnosis may require imaging, blood tests, lung function tests or a biopsy.
Not everyone with sarcoidosis requires medication; management depends on the organs affected and disease severity.
Attend recommended follow-up appointments to monitor organ function.
Avoid smoking and discuss suitable lifestyle measures with your healthcare professional.
Do not start steroid or immune-suppressing medicines without medical supervision.
urgent_warning_signs: New irregular heartbeat accompanied by dizziness or weakness
Sudden vision changes or severe eye pain

Pancreatic neoplasm.overview: A pancreatic neoplasm is an abnormal growth in the pancreas. It may be benign or malignant. Pancreatic cancer is a malignant pancreatic neoplasm. Symptoms may be absent in the early stages and can overlap with several digestive conditions. A medical assessment is required to determine the nature of a growth.
common_symptoms: Pain that may spread to the back
Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice)
general_guidance: Seek medical assessment for unexplained weight loss, persistent abdominal pain or jaundice.
A healthcare professional may recommend blood tests and imaging investigations.
Further assessment or a biopsy may be required to identify the type of pancreatic growth.
Follow the investigation and treatment plan provided by the specialist team.
Symptoms alone cannot confirm pancreatic cancer or distinguish benign from malignant growths.
Do not delay medical assessment if symptoms persist or worsen.
urgent_warning_signs: Yellowing of the skin or whites of the eyes
Persistent vomiting or inability to keep fluids down

Pericarditis.overview: Pericarditis is inflammation of the pericardium, the protective sac surrounding the heart. It commonly causes sharp or stabbing chest pain that may worsen during deep breathing or while lying down and may improve when sitting up and leaning forward. Chest pain must be medically assessed because it can also indicate a heart attack or another serious condition.
common_symptoms: Chest pain that worsens when breathing deeply
Pain that worsens when lying down
Pain that improves when sitting up or leaning forward
Pain spreading to the shoulders, arms or abdomen
general_guidance: Seek medical assessment for chest pain, even if it appears to improve with a change in posture.
A healthcare professional may recommend an ECG, blood tests, chest X-ray or echocardiogram.
Treatment depends on the cause and may involve prescribed anti-inflammatory medicines or other treatment.
Avoid strenuous physical activity until a healthcare professional advises that it is safe to resume.
Follow the prescribed treatment and monitoring plan.
Do not assume chest pain is pericarditis without appropriate medical evaluation.
urgent_warning_signs: Chest pain spreading to the arms, back, neck or jaw
Chest pain accompanied by sweating, nausea or shortness of breath
